title: For an affine morphism, an ideal times a direct image is the direct image of the pulled-back ideal times the module
statement: Let $f:Y\to X$ be an affine morphism of schemes [pqf-def-affine-morphism], $\mathcal F$ a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_Y$-module and $\mathcal I\subseteq\mathcal O_X$ a quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals [pqf-def-coherent]. Let $f_*$ and $f^*$ be the direct image and pullback of modules [def-pc-module-pullback], and $\epsilon_f:f^*\mathcal O_X\to\mathcal O_Y$ the morphism adjoint to $f^\sharp$ [lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-structure-sheaf]. Define $f^{-1}\mathcal I\cdot\mathcal F\subseteq\mathcal F$ as the image of the composite $f^*\mathcal I\otimes_{\mathcal O_Y}\mathcal F\to f^*\mathcal O_X\otimes_{\mathcal O_Y}\mathcal F\to\mathcal O_Y\otimes_{\mathcal O_Y}\mathcal F\to\mathcal F$ (pullback of the inclusion $\mathcal I\subseteq\mathcal O_X$, then $\epsilon_f\otimes\mathrm{id}$, then multiplication; tensor products as in [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]), and $\mathcal I\cdot f_*\mathcal F\subseteq f_*\mathcal F$ as the image of the multiplication map $\mathcal I\otimes_{\mathcal O_X}f_*\mathcal F\to f_*\mathcal F$. Then (1) $f^{-1}\mathcal I\cdot\mathcal F$ is a quasi-coherent sub-$\mathcal O_Y$-module of $\mathcal F$; (2) $\mathcal I\cdot f_*\mathcal F=f_*(f^{-1}\mathcal I\cdot\mathcal F)$ as sub-$\mathcal O_X$-modules of $f_*\mathcal F$.

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma 01YP (label lemma-affine-morphism-projection-ideal, coherent.tex line 3523): clause (2) is the statement; clause (1) is said in the first paragraph of its proof and is used as a fact by Lemma 01YQ ('as pointed out in the proof of Lemma ...'), so it is stated here

proof.text: (Clause (1).) Write $\iota:\mathcal I\to\mathcal O_X$ for the inclusion and $\psi:f^*\mathcal I\otimes_{\mathcal O_Y}\mathcal F\to\mathcal F$ for the composite $\mu\circ(\epsilon_f\otimes\mathrm{id})\circ(f^*\iota\otimes\mathrm{id})$ of the statement, where $\mu:\mathcal O_Y\otimes_{\mathcal O_Y}\mathcal F\to\mathcal F$ is the multiplication; $f^*\iota$ is $\mathcal O_Y$-linear because $f^*$ is a functor of modules [def-pc-module-pullback], $\epsilon_f$ is $\mathcal O_Y$-linear [lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-structure-sheaf], and a tensor product $u\otimes v$ of $\mathcal O_Y$-linear maps and $\mu$ are the $\mathcal O_Y$-linear maps of sheafifications [def-weil-pbc-sheafification] induced by the presheaf maps $x\otimes s\mapsto u_U(x)\otimes v_U(s)$ and $b\otimes s\mapsto bs$ on $U\mapsto\mathcal G(U)\otimes_{\mathcal O_Y(U)}\mathcal H(U)$ [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. Hence $\psi$ is a morphism of $\mathcal O_Y$-modules and $f^{-1}\mathcal I\cdot\mathcal F=\operatorname{Im}\psi$. Its source is quasi-coherent: $f^*\mathcal I$ is quasi-coherent [lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-quasi-coherent] since $\mathcal I$ is, and the tensor product of the quasi-coherent modules $f^*\mathcal I$ and $\mathcal F$ is quasi-coherent [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-tensor-product-affine-sections]; its target $\mathcal F$ is quasi-coherent. So $\operatorname{Im}\psi=f^{-1}\mathcal I\cdot\mathcal F$ is a quasi-coherent sub-$\mathcal O_Y$-module of $\mathcal F$, with $(f^{-1}\mathcal I\cdot\mathcal F)(U)=\psi_U\big((f^*\mathcal I\otimes_{\mathcal O_Y}\mathcal F)(U)\big)$ for every affine open $U\subseteq Y$ [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-module-cokernel-image] (1)-(3). This is (1). In Lean, compare tensorPullback with Mathlib pullback using uniqueness of left adjoints, transfer quasi-coherence across this natural isomorphism, and transfer the abelian-image quasi-coherence through Abelian.imageIsoImage to the chosen categorical image.

proof.text: (The map $\psi$ on sections over an affine preimage.) Let $V\subseteq X$ be an affine open, $A=\mathcal O_X(V)$. Since $f$ is affine [pqf-def-affine-morphism], $U=f^{-1}(V)$ is an affine open of $Y$; put $B=\mathcal O_Y(U)$ and $\rho=f^\sharp_V:A\to B$. Let $t_U:(f^*\mathcal I)(U)\otimes_B\mathcal F(U)\to(f^*\mathcal I\otimes_{\mathcal O_Y}\mathcal F)(U)$ be the component of the sheafification map, bijective since $U$ is affine and both factors are quasi-coherent (step 1, [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-tensor-product-affine-sections]), and $c:\mathcal I(V)\otimes_AB\to(f^*\mathcal I)(U)$, $a\otimes b\mapsto b\cdot\eta_{\mathcal I}(a)|_U$, the $B$-linear bijection of [lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-affine-sections] (with $\eta$ the unit of $f^*\dashv f_*$ [def-pc-module-pullback]). Claim: for $a\in\mathcal I(V)$, $b\in B$, $s\in\mathcal F(U)$, $\psi_U\big(t_U(c(a\otimes b)\otimes s)\big)=b\,\rho(a)\,s$. Indeed, by the description of $u\otimes v$ and $\mu$ in step 1 (naturality of the sheafification map [def-weil-pbc-sheafification]), $\psi_U(t_U(x\otimes s))=\big(\epsilon_{f,U}((f^*\iota)_U(x))\big)\,s$ for $x\in(f^*\mathcal I)(U)$. Naturality of the unit gives $(f^*\iota)(\eta_{\mathcal I}(a))=\eta_{\mathcal O_X}(\iota(a))=\eta_{\mathcal O_X}(a)$, and $\epsilon_f(\eta_{\mathcal O_X}(a))=f^\sharp_V(a)=\rho(a)$ in $\mathcal O_Y(f^{-1}V)=B$ by the characterization of $\epsilon_f$ in [lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-structure-sheaf]. As $(f^*\iota)_U$ and $\epsilon_{f,U}$ are $B$-linear, $\epsilon_{f,U}((f^*\iota)_U(c(a\otimes b)))=b\,\rho(a)$, which gives the claim.

proof.text: (Sections of $f^{-1}\mathcal I\cdot\mathcal F$ over $U=f^{-1}(V)$.) Notation of step 2; regard $M=\mathcal F(U)$ as an $A$-module through $\rho$, and let $\mathcal I(V)M$ be the $A$-submodule generated by the products $a\cdot s=\rho(a)s$, $a\in\mathcal I(V)$, $s\in M$. Since $c$ and $t_U$ are surjective and $\mathcal I(V)\otimes_AB$, $(f^*\mathcal I)(U)\otimes_BM$ are additively generated by pure tensors, the elements $t_U(c(a\otimes b)\otimes s)$ additively generate $(f^*\mathcal I\otimes_{\mathcal O_Y}\mathcal F)(U)$. By step 2, $\psi_U$ maps them to $b\rho(a)s=\rho(a)(bs)\in\mathcal I(V)M$, and every generator $\rho(a)s$ of $\mathcal I(V)M$ is such an image ($b=1$). Hence, by step 1, $(f^{-1}\mathcal I\cdot\mathcal F)(U)=\psi_U((f^*\mathcal I\otimes\mathcal F)(U))=\mathcal I(V)\,\mathcal F(U)$ inside $\mathcal F(U)$. (This is the identity $I(M_A)=((IB)M)_A$ of the source: $(IB)M=IM$.) The private product_range_affine helper proves the needed product-section formula for any map to the structure sheaf: use the affine tensor-section bijection, the image-section equality and tensor induction to identify its range with the additive subgroup generated by products. It does not require that the map be mono, so it applies to the extended ideal map as well.

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma 01YP (coherent-lemma-affine-morphism-projection-ideal, coherent.tex line 3523), proof, second paragraph, the identity I(M_A) = ((IB)M)_A

proof.text: (The direct images.) An affine morphism is quasi-compact and quasi-separated [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence] (3), so $f_*\mathcal F$ is a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module [pqf-lem-pushforward-qcoh]. By the definition of the pushforward [def-pc-module-pullback], $(f_*\mathcal F)(W)=\mathcal F(f^{-1}W)$ for opens $W\subseteq X$, with the restrictions of $\mathcal F$ and $a\in\mathcal O_X(W)$ acting as $f^\sharp_W(a)$; in particular $(f_*\mathcal F)(V)$ is $M=\mathcal F(f^{-1}V)$ with $A$ acting through $\rho$ (notation of step 2). For the sub-$\mathcal O_Y$-module $f^{-1}\mathcal I\cdot\mathcal F\subseteq\mathcal F$ (step 1), $f_*(f^{-1}\mathcal I\cdot\mathcal F)$ is the sub-$\mathcal O_X$-module $W\mapsto(f^{-1}\mathcal I\cdot\mathcal F)(f^{-1}W)$ of $f_*\mathcal F$ (stable under $f^\sharp_W(a)$ since it is an $\mathcal O_Y$-submodule). By step 3, $f_*(f^{-1}\mathcal I\cdot\mathcal F)(V)=\mathcal I(V)M$ for every affine open $V\subseteq X$.

proof.text: For the downstairs product, apply the same product_range_affine computation directly to the original inclusion and the quasi-coherent pushforward. The multiplication map sends a tensor to its scalar action by the section of the structure sheaf (TensorSection.whiskerRight_app_tmulSection and leftUnitor_hom_app_tmulSection). Surjectivity of the affine tensor comparison and tensor induction identify the image range with the additive subgroup generated by these products. The pushforward action is through the ring map f.app V. Thus its subgroup is exactly the upstairs subgroup computed in step 3. This avoids converting the arbitrary inclusion into bundled IdealSheafData and does not use the ideal-times-quasi-coherent-affine-sections lemma.

proof.text: Affine opens form a basis. If monomorphisms i:M→P and j:N→P have equal section ranges on all affine opens, then i followed by the cokernel projection of j vanishes on each affine open. The private hom_zero_of_affine helper uses affine opens contained in any given open, naturality, and sheaf separatedness to prove this composite vanishes everywhere. Lift i through kernel(cokernel.π j), which is Abelian.image j, and compose with the inverse of Abelian.factorThruImage j (an isomorphism since j is mono). This produces a factorization through j and therefore Subobject.mk i ≤ Subobject.mk j. Reverse their roles for equality. The ideal-product inclusion is mono and pushforward preserves monos, so imageSubobject_mono identifies both images in the conclusion with these subobjects. All kernel lifts, image factors, and subobject inequalities are proved with Mathlib.
